2. The plaint case is that, the defendant was a monthly tenant at a rental of Taka 400.00 per month with effect from 1-8-81. At the time of execution of the agreement the plaintiff took an advance of Taka 14,000.00 with a condition that Taka 100.00 will be adjusted from the rent every month. The petitioner defaulted in paying rent from April, 1984 to September, 1993 for 114 months and filed House Rent Deposit Control Case No. 159 of 1993. The defendant paid Taka 33,000.00 in three installments. A solenama was filed in Rent Deposit Control Case No. 159 of 1993 which having not been supported by the parties was rejected and the rent deposit case was dismissed. Thereafter, the defendant defaulted in payment of rent from October, 1993, After serving a notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act on 18-1-95 the suit was filed. 

 3. The defendant asserted that the suit premises were let out to him in 1981 at a rental of Taka 400.00 and he paid Taka 14,000.00 as advance. The defendant further asserted that although an advance of Taka 14,000.00 was lying with the plaintiff he illegally demanded one lac taka on 1-8-93 and wanted to evict the defendant forcibly. The defendant filed OC Suit No. 181 of 1993 which was dismissed on contest. As the plaintiff refused to accept rent the defendant filed House Rent Control Case No. 159 of 1993 wherein a solenama was filed by both the parties mentioning about realization of Taka 10,000.00 as advance. This solenama was not accepted and the case was dismissed. The further case of the defendant is that in OC Suit No. 181 of 1993. DW I, the son of the plaintiff, admitted about the payment of arrear rents on compromise and also about the payment of advance money. According to the defendant, he is not a defaulter as the advance was lying with the plaintiff which was sufficient to adjust the rent up to March, 1996. The defendant further asserted that the notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act is not sufficient. 

 4. Mr Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-tenant petitioner, submits first that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division failed to appreciate and construe Ext. Gha (2), the solenama, in its true perspective wherein the payment of advance money of Taka 10,000.00 was admitted, resulting in an error in the decision wherein the learned Single Judge wrongly held that the payment of advance was not proved. He next submits that notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act is insufficient as the agreement contemplates a notice of three months and the learned Single Judge wrongly held that one month's notice is sufficient in the case of eviction of the defendant.
